test.name: Planning request must not run a full-text search
test.description: User asks what to research next — a planning request, not an execution request. search-full-text executes plan items; it does not generate plans or questions. On an empty project the right destination is the question-selection agent; once a question is active it is research-plan. Graded on the no-harm invariant (no fulltext_search call) rather than on routing: a routed negative counts Skill calls only, so the correct agent spawn could never satisfy a routing check (issue #2115).

input.user_message: I'm just starting a project on Patrick Flynn (b. ca. 1845, PA; d. 1908, Schuylkill Co.). Help me figure out the right opening research questions to scope this — I haven't written any plans or questions yet. Don't run any searches.

negative.explanation: The user is asking for planning advice, not asking for a specific search to be executed. The gate is the deterministic validator test_no_fulltext_search_on_planning_request (eval/harness/validators/test_search_full_text.py), which runs via the `no-fulltext-search` tag and fails the run on any fulltext_search call. research-plan stays listed as an acceptable Skill route; spawning the question-selection agent, the right opener on an empty project, is equally acceptable and is why routing does not decide this test.

judge_context: This test is graded on the no-harm invariant, NOT on routing (`grade_on_invariant: true`): no fulltext_search call may be issued without a plan item to anchor it.

Routing to research-plan, or delegating to the question-selection agent to derive the opening question, are both acceptable — the user is asking what to ask and search next, which is planning territory.
May briefly explain the difference between planning and executing a search if it helps the genealogist understand the routing.
